$description: The Health OS reference catalogue. One entry per token group, component, widget, pattern and asset library: what it is for, when to use it, when not to, and its API. The reference site renders these entries next to each live example, and scripts/docs.mjs generates design-system/REFERENCE.md from the same file, so the site and the written reference never disagree. Edit here, then run `npm run docs`.

sections.lead: Tokens, components and voice, documented and ready to build with.

sections.title: Overview

checklist: Every colour, size, radius, shadow and duration comes from a token. No hex codes or pixel values typed by hand.
The page uses one theme: light or paper.
Headings use the heading or subheading role, running text uses body, small text uses label.
Rose, apricot and lavender appear only in their 50, 400 and 700 shades. Status colours report real states only.
At most one gradient moment per view, using one of the three gradients.
There is one primary button per view. Other actions are secondary or text.
Cards are the right type for their job: content, feature, service, pricing, resource or action.
Images come from the tagged library, match their suggested use, and text never sits on a raw photo.
Screenshots are cropped to the point, framed on a surface, and show no private or client information.
Copy is plain Australian English in sentence case, with no em dashes and no invented numbers.
Prices, offers and claims match the Health OS database. No testimonials, countdown pressure or before-and-after images.
Motion is calm, and nothing people need is hidden until an animation finishes.
Anything outside the system has a defined need, is documented, and has Tumai's approval.

open.question: Keep md 8px, lg 12px and full, or return to the earlier 8px cap?
open.current: Provisional: md 8px for controls, lg 12px for containers, full for round things only. No pill buttons.

open.question: Approve rose-700 as the brand primary fill, with carbon as the neutral primary?
open.current: rose-700 #97215F with white text. The old rose-600 #BE2E7B step was removed by the three-shade rule.

open.question: Which word does copy use for the customer: operator, practitioner or something else?
open.current: The database says operator. Demo copy in this system says you and clients, and names neither.

open.question: Sage 70 / Creator 30, or Creator 70 / Explorer 30?
open.current: Not used anywhere in this system until decided.

open.question: Which filled icon set, in which two sizes?
open.current: The Icons section is intentionally empty. Components still use Lucide line icons until the set is chosen.

open.question: What should motion do when someone has reduced motion switched on?
open.current: Unchanged from before the cleanup: loops stop and entrances settle instantly. Not an approved policy.

open.question: Commission a true vector mark, and decide whether a wordmark lockup exists?
open.current: The 500px PNG mark is the only usable file. The SVG embeds PNG rasters and is not a vector.

open.question: Polish, keep or delete the five experimental widgets?
open.current: 05 Live session timer, 08 Countdown, 29 Rating summary, 30 Assistant message and 31 Check-in are on and labelled.

open.question: Keep the stack comparison pattern alongside the database rule on comparisons?
open.current: Kept without competitor names or prices. It compares a typical stack of separate tools with one system.

open.question: Act on the tagging notes, or keep everything exactly as it is?
open.current: All 169 images kept. Notes flag 17 byte-identical pairs, visible third-party lettering, two photos showing a Health OS cap and some off-palette backgrounds.

open.question: Keep Certified, Therapeutic grade and Ethically sourced as badge examples?
open.current: Kept as requested. Use them only for a business's own verifiable facts, never as a claim about Health OS.

open.question: Replace the coded dashboard preview with a real, cropped product screenshot?
open.current: The command hero shows a coded mock of the dashboard with sample data.

entries.name: Brand colours
entries.purpose: Rose, apricot and lavender: the Health OS identity. Each has three shades: 50 soft, 400 base, 700 deep.
use: 50 for tinted backgrounds: badges, selected rows, soft fills
400 for the brand DNA: gradient stops, decorative marks, chart fills
700 for coloured text, links, icons and filled buttons with white text
avoid: Text in a 400 shade, or white text on a 400 fill
Shades outside 50, 400 and 700
Using all three colours with equal weight in one small component
entries.api: Tailwind: bg-rose-50, text-rose-700, border-apricot-400, from-lavender-400 … CSS: var(--hos-rose-700)

entries.name: Neutrals
entries.purpose: Warm greys for text, lines and quiet fills, plus carbon for the one dark surface.
use: ink-900 headings and primary text, ink-600 body, ink-500 secondary text
ink-100 and ink-200 for quiet fills, dividers and pressed states
carbon for neutral primary buttons, the footer panel and dark tiles, with white text
avoid: ink-400 for text people need to read
Pure black or hand-coded white as a page ground
entries.api: text-ink-900 · text-ink-600 · text-ink-500 · bg-ink-100 · border-line · bg-carbon · text-white

entries.name: Status colours
entries.purpose: Success, warning and error, kept apart from the brand colours.
use: 100 tint behind status content
700 for status text
600 for icons and dots
avoid: Decorating with status colours when nothing is succeeding, pending or failing
Using error red as a brand accent
entries.api: bg-success-100 text-success-700 · bg-warning-100 text-warning-700 · bg-error-100 text-error-700

entries.name: Themes: light and paper
entries.purpose: Two themes that share every colour, component and behaviour. Only the grounds change.
use: Light (default) for product UI and crisp marketing pages
Paper (.theme-paper on <html>) for reading-led pages: warm ivory with a faint paper grain
Surfaces through bg-paper, bg-surface, bg-surface-2 and border-line so both themes work
avoid: Mixing themes within one page
Hard-coding a ground colour: it breaks the other theme
A dark theme: there isn't one

entries.name: Signature gradient
entries.purpose: Apricot to rose to lavender. The strongest brand moment.
use: The logo
One gradient panel, bar or button per view
Progress fills and selected states in widgets
avoid: Large text-heavy areas
More than one gradient moment in a view
Reversing or recolouring the stops

entries.name: Soft wash
entries.purpose: The three 50 tints in a gentle wash. The quiet gradient.
use: Large calm fills: section panels, media placeholders, the featured pricing header
The highlight behind one headline word (.text-highlight)
avoid: Behind small light text
Every card on a page

entries.name: Warm sunrise
entries.purpose: Apricot into rose. The inviting gradient.
use: Action cards and promotional bands
A warm highlight (.text-highlight-warm) when the soft wash is too quiet
avoid: Status or error meaning
Pairing with the signature gradient in the same view

entries.name: Heading
entries.purpose: One heading size, Spline Sans 700, fluid from 36px to 58px.
use: Page titles, section titles and hero headlines
A single large figure
avoid: Card titles: use subheading
More than one heading size on a page

entries.name: Subheading
entries.purpose: Spline Sans 600, fluid from 20px to 24px.
use: Card titles and group titles inside a section
Compact figures in widgets
avoid: Running text
Stacking two subheadings without body between

entries.name: Body
entries.purpose: Anonymous Pro 400, 16px on 26px. The Health OS texture.
use: All running text, descriptions, inputs and table cells
Button labels, set in the display family
avoid: Lines longer than about 70 characters: use max-w-reading
Bold paragraphs

entries.name: Label
entries.purpose: Anonymous Pro 700 at 12px. Small text, only where needed.
use: Badges, table headers and chart axes
Metadata such as dates and reading time
Eyebrows above headings, in uppercase, at most one per three sections
avoid: Sentences or paragraphs
Anything smaller than label

entries.name: Spacing
entries.purpose: An 8px rhythm with 4px steps for tight spots. The same spacing in both themes.
use: 8px steps (2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24) for layout, sections and cards
4px steps (1, 3, 5) for icon gaps, badge padding and dense controls
Section padding py-16 on phones, py-24 on desktop; hero-py tokens for heroes
avoid: Half steps such as 0.5, 1.5, 2.5 and 3.5
Typed pixel values such as mt-[13px]
entries.api: p-6 · gap-4 · py-24 · pt-hero-py md:pt-hero-py-lg · mt-hero-gap

entries.name: Radius
entries.purpose: Three corner sizes.
use: md (8px) for controls: buttons, inputs, chips, badges, icon wells
lg (12px) for containers: cards, panels, dialogs, media frames
full for round things: avatars, dots, toggles and the theme switch
avoid: Pill-shaped buttons
Mixing md and lg on the same kind of element

entries.name: Shadow
entries.purpose: Three soft, neutral elevations. Surfaces are flat with a hairline by default.
use: sm for hover lift on cards
md for floating UI: menus, tooltips, toasts
lg for dialogs and framed previews
avoid: Coloured or glowing shadows
A shadow on every resting card

entries.name: Motion tokens
entries.purpose: Durations and easings that keep custom motion consistent.
use: xs 80ms taps, sm 160ms hovers, md 240ms cards and menus
lg 360ms reveals, xl 480ms signature moments
ease-out for arrivals, ease-standard for state changes
avoid: Bouncy or elastic easing
Motion that hides content until it finishes

entries.name: Logo
entries.purpose: The gradient OS mark, shipped as a PNG.
use: On its own, on light, paper or carbon
Clear space of at least a quarter of its width on every side
16px minimum, for favicons
avoid: Recolouring, outlining, stretching or adding effects
Placing it on a busy photo without a surface behind it

entries.name: Icon library
entries.purpose: One filled icon set in two sizes: small and large. Being rebuilt.
use: Until the set is approved, components keep their current icons
avoid: Adding a second icon style in the meantime
Mixing outline and filled icons in new work

entries.name: Button
entries.purpose: The standard action in three styles.
use: primary for the one main action in a view (tone neutral when rose would clash)
secondary beside a primary for the alternative
text for low-emphasis actions inside copy, cards and rows
size small only in dense areas: tables, toolbars, cards
avoid: Two primary buttons in one view
Custom colours, gradients or pill shapes
A button for navigation inside running text: use a link
entries.api: variant: primary | secondary | text · tone: brand | neutral · size: default | small · loading · disabled · href · leadingIcon · trailingIcon

entries.name: Icon button
entries.purpose: An icon-only action that mirrors the three button styles.
use: Toolbars, headers, media controls, close and menu
Always with an aria-label
avoid: Actions people won't recognise from the icon alone: use a Button with a label
entries.api: variant: primary | secondary | text · tone · size: default | small · aria-label (required)

entries.name: Badge
entries.purpose: A soft tag for status, category and topic.
use: neutral and outline for quiet tags
rose, apricot and lavender for brand categories
success, warning and error only for a real state
avoid: Badges as buttons
More than three badges on one card
entries.api: variant: neutral | outline | rose | apricot | lavender | success | warning | error · size: sm | md · emoji · dot

entries.purpose: The small uppercase label that gives context: an eyebrow, a numbered step, a live state.
